calls.question: Will CEE/CIS primary bond issuance volume increase over the next month?
calls.forecast: Most signals point to steady-to-softer CEE/CIS primary issuance over the next month, as sovereigns like Poland, Hungary and Romania have front-loaded 2026 funding and are leaning on liability management (switches/taps) rather than fresh benchmark supply. There's a real but minority risk that tight spreads and rollover pressure (notably Romania and Turkish sukuk) tempt issuers into opportunistic taps, which keeps the probability from falling lower. Overall, a modest pickup can't be ruled out, but the base case favors flat-to-lower volumes.

calls.question: Will telecom-embedded financial services see a major new partnership or launch this month?
calls.forecast: Telecom-embedded finance has produced a major partnership or launch roughly every 3-6 weeks since early 2026 (VEON, Circles/Airwallex, Ericsson/Mastercard, Visa/Telefonica), and that promotional cadence plus broad 'major' criteria make another qualifying announcement this month likely. Some uncertainty remains since a few recent items may be recycled news rather than genuinely new deals, so the outcome isn't a lock, but the base rate strongly favors a yes.

calls.question: Will discussion intensity around AI regulation increase over the next week?
calls.forecast: Multiple active pressure points—200+ state lawmaker letters, Blackburn-White House text negotiations, and 1,500+ pending state bills—point toward rising discussion intensity as stakeholders race to lock in positions before the recess deadline. The main caveat is that the Obernolte-Trahan proposal remains a discussion draft rather than a scheduled vote, which could cap escalation short of a full spike, but historical pre-recess dynamics favor increased commentary over a plateau. Net expectation: discussion volume rises meaningfully this week.
